articles.title: MMX lifts off to Mars’s moon Phobos
articles.description:
Image:
			MMX lifts off to Mars’s moon Phobos
articles.summary: The Martian Moons eXploration (MMX) mission launches toward Phobos, marking a landmark journey to explore Mars' mysterious moon.

articles.title: Rubin observatory reveals two hidden companions of the Milky Way
articles.description: Preview data from the recently completed NSF-DOE Vera C. Rubin Observatory in Chile point to a wave of discoveries that may complete the census of the Milky Way's neighboring galaxies—including its faintest companions.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: The Vera C. Rubin Observatory has discovered two previously hidden companion galaxies orbiting the Milky Way, opening the door to major new discoveries about our galactic neighborhood. This breakthrough from preview data promises groundbreaking insights into galactic structure and dynamics.

articles.title: Smithsonian scientists just recreated the first 2 billion years of the Universe
articles.description: Scientists have created one of the largest and most detailed simulations of the early universe ever made, offering an extraordinary new glimpse into the cosmos shortly after the Big Bang. Called Lumina, the groundbreaking simulation recreates the universe’s first 2 billion years, showing how dark matter, gas, and radiation interacted to give rise to the earliest stars, galaxies, and black holes.
articles.summary: Smithsonian scientists have created one of the largest and most detailed simulations of the early universe, modeling the first 2 billion years of cosmic history. This achievement provides unprecedented insights into the universe's origin and evolution.

articles.title: Three giant black holes discovered in a galaxy from the dawn of time
articles.description: Astronomers have discovered three actively feeding black holes inside a single galaxy more than 12.5 billion light-years away, revealing a remarkable scene from the universe’s infancy. Two of the black holes are separated by just 620 light-years and are expected to eventually merge, while a third lurks farther away. One weighs an astonishing 80 million suns, and another is growing faster than conventional theories predict.
articles.summary: Astronomers have discovered three actively feeding supermassive black holes within a single galaxy dating back more than 12.5 billion years to the dawn of time. This remarkable finding challenges theories about early galaxy formation and black hole evolution.

articles.title: Rubin Observatory Spots Possible Dwarf Planet Beyond Pluto—the Biggest in 20 Years
articles.description: The distant, icy celestial body could be our solar system's sixth dwarf planet.
articles.summary: Rubin Observatory has identified a possible dwarf planet beyond Pluto, marking the largest such discovery in 20 years and potentially adding a sixth dwarf planet to our solar system.

articles.title: Giant new dwarf planet discovered in our own solar system — hiding in plain sight
articles.description: A large object in the Kuiper Belt — a distant region of icy and rocky bodies past Neptune — appears to be a new candidate dwarf planet.
articles.summary: A large icy object discovered in the Kuiper Belt appears to be a new dwarf planet candidate, hidden in plain sight in our own solar system.

articles.title: Map Showing Potential Origins of Martian Meteorite Teghaza 001
articles.description: Description This global map of Mars shows 13 locations that match the mineralogy and chemistry of Teghaza 001, one of the most ancient Martian meteorites ever found on Earth. While scientists can never know for sure where a Martian meteorite originated, Teghaza 001 includes clues that link it to highlands in the southern hemisphere of […]
articles.summary: A global map of Mars identifies 13 locations matching the mineralogy and chemistry of the ancient Martian meteorite Teghaza 001, aiding scientific understanding of Mars' geology.

articles.title: Slice of Martian Meteorite Teghaza 001
articles.description: Description This slice of Teghaza 001, one of the most ancient Martian meteorites ever found on Earth, was used to determine the age of the rock. Reflected light images like these serve as a scientist’s road map, helping them find minerals of interest to analyze by different instruments. Figure A is the same image with […]
articles.summary: Analysis of Teghaza 001, one of the most ancient Martian meteorites ever found on Earth, reveals crucial insights into Mars' early geological history.

articles.title: NASA-funded Study Details One of Oldest Mars Meteorites Ever Found
articles.description: When a rose-colored meteorite was found in the Sahara Desert in 2022, no one knew how old it was or where it came from. Not until NASA-funded scientists age-dated its minerals did they realize the nearly 2-pound (800-gram) rock was a piece of Mars that formed more than 4.1 billion years ago, making it one […]
articles.summary: A NASA-funded study reveals the age and origin of Teghaza 001, a rose-colored meteorite found in the Sahara Desert that ranks among Mars' oldest known samples.

articles.title: Ghostly Cat’s Head Nebula lurks within sight of Hubble and Webb
articles.description: The NASA/ESA Hubble and the NASA/ESA/CSA James Webb Space Telescopes recently stared at an eerie star-forming scene within the Carina Nebula, a massive gas and dust cloud located approximately 7500 light-years away from Earth. The two telescopes offer complementary views of the shadowy form, nicknamed the Cat’s Head Nebula, which reflects the 'magical'' process of star formation. Hubble’s visible-light view shows the cat as a dark, elongated dust pillar and hints of young forming stars, while Webb’s infrared-light imagery unveils many stars and other hidden details.
articles.summary: Hubble and James Webb Space Telescopes jointly observe the Cat's Head Nebula, revealing a spectacular star-forming region with unprecedented detail.

articles.title: Celebrating BepiColombo, three words at a time
articles.description:
Video: 
			00:03:32
				
BepiColombo launched on 20 October 2018. This year, the anniversary is special. After eight years of travelling through the inner Solar System, the ESA/JAXA mission will arrive at Mercury on 9 December, 2026. To celebrate, mission team members were asked to describe BepiColombo in just three words.
Their answers capture the character of the mission and the people behind it. Complex, collaborative and transformative are among the words chosen, reflecting both the demanding journey to Mercury and the international teamwork that has made it possible. Together, their words offer a personal snapshot of BepiColombo as it approaches its long-awaited destination.
articles.summary: BepiColombo celebrates eight years of pioneering exploration to Mercury, advancing our understanding of the innermost planet.

articles.title: Euclid discovers new comet
articles.description: The European Space Agency’s Euclid space telescope has discovered its first previously unknown comet, in images taken between 16 and 24 September 2026.
articles.summary: The European Space Agency's Euclid space telescope discovers a previously unknown comet, expanding humanity's catalog of solar system objects.

articles.title: Mars moon lander set to launch on 19 October
articles.description:
The Martian Moons eXploration (MMX) mission is set to launch into space on a H3 rocket from the Tanegashima Space Center at 04:41 JST on 20 October 2026 (20:41 BST / 21:41 CEST on 19 October 2026). MMX will be the first mission to collect a sample from Mars’s moon Phobos and bring it back to Earth. 
MMX is led by the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA), in collaboration with the National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA), the French space agency (CNES), the German Aerospace Center (DLR) and the European Space Agency (ESA).
articles.summary: The Martian Moons eXploration (MMX) mission prepares for launch on an H3 rocket, embarking on an ambitious expedition to explore Mars' intriguing moons.

articles.title: Solar Orbiter tracks origin of mysterious magnetic switchbacks
articles.description: The European Space Agency-led Solar Orbiter spacecraft has flown through an S-shaped kink known as a ‘switchback’ in the solar wind’s magnetic field. By fingerprinting the elusive particles within the switchback, Solar Orbiter has traced its origin back to the Sun’s surface and revealed more about solar magnetism – the unruly instigator of dangerous solar storms.
articles.summary: Solar Orbiter has discovered and tracked S-shaped magnetic switchbacks in the Sun's corona, advancing our understanding of solar magnetic phenomena and particle acceleration.

articles.title: No Comets Required? How the Growing Earth May Have Created Its Own Water
articles.description: Earth may not have needed comets and asteroids to deliver its water after it formed and cooled. Instead, water creation could have been part of the planet's formation process. New research explains how, and even shows that water creation could be a part of every rocky planet's formation.
articles.summary: New research suggests Earth may have generated its own water through chemical processes rather than requiring delivery by comets and asteroids.

articles.title: Colliding Dwarf Planets Created a 'Cat's Tail' 1,000 Astronomical Units Long
articles.description: The Beta Pictoris system is only about 63 light years away. At only about 23 million years old, it's a sort of analogue for our Solar System when it was much younger. Observations show an elongated dust feature named the 'Cat's Tail' that has puzzled researchers. New research says it's the result of two colliding dwarf planets, something that was sure to have happened in our Solar System when it was young.
articles.summary: A collision between dwarf planets in the Beta Pictoris system created a dramatic debris structure extending 1,000 astronomical units, revealing planetary collision dynamics.

articles.title: NASA's new UV space telescope will launch in 2031
articles.description: Most of us could spend our entire lives looking at the night sky and see very few changes. The moon becomes more or less illuminated, the planets drift placidly through the sky, satellites and the ISS intrude for a few moments at a time, and the bright, momentary streak of a meteor punctuates the occasional evening of stargazing.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: NASA's next-generation ultraviolet space telescope will launch in 2031, opening new windows for observing the cosmos.

articles.title: Rare 4.1-billion-year-old Martian meteorite reveals clues to planet's ancient past
articles.description: Scientists at the University of New Mexico have played a key role in identifying a rare, 4.1-billion-year-old Martian meteorite that provides new evidence that the red planet may have once had a wetter, Earth-like environment.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: A rare 4.1-billion-year-old Martian meteorite provides unprecedented clues to Mars' ancient geological history and habitability.

articles.title: Built to take the blast: Students test prototype landing pad to make moon landings safer
articles.description: As NASA works toward a sustained human presence on the moon, researchers at The University of Alabama in Huntsville (UAH), a part of The University of Alabama System, are helping solve one of the most pressing challenges facing future lunar missions: how to land spacecraft safely without damaging the landing vehicle or nearby infrastructure.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: University of Alabama researchers are developing prototype landing pads to improve safety for NASA's upcoming sustained lunar missions. This innovation supports the agency's ambitious goals for human presence on the Moon.

articles.title: Einstein's equations may explain the universe without dark energy
articles.description: Mathematicians have uncovered what they argue is a fundamental flaw in the standard model of the universe, potentially challenging the need for dark energy. Their calculations suggest that the mathematical framework used to describe cosmic expansion is inherently unstable and that the universe could accelerate naturally under Einstein's original theory of gravity. The findings also raise surprising questions about whether our location in the universe is as ordinary as scientists have long assumed.
articles.summary: Mathematicians have identified a potential fundamental flaw in the standard cosmological model, suggesting Einstein's equations may explain the universe without requiring dark energy. This theoretical breakthrough could reshape our understanding of cosmic structure and evolution.

articles.title: NASA discovers Jupiter’s invisible shield is more complex than Earth’s
articles.description: NASA’s Juno spacecraft has discovered that Jupiter uses a surprisingly complex system of powerful plasma waves and multiple shock regions to defend against the solar wind. The findings reveal major differences between Jupiter and Earth and could help scientists understand the enormous shock waves produced by exploding stars.
articles.summary: NASA's Juno spacecraft reveals that Jupiter's magnetosphere is far more complex than Earth's, utilizing powerful plasma waves and multiple protective mechanisms. This discovery deepens our understanding of planetary protection and magnetic field dynamics.

articles.title: NASA’s Artemis I mission reveals surprising radiation levels near the Moon
articles.description: NASA’s Artemis I mission has revealed that cosmic radiation near the Moon is higher than in Earth orbit, but not by as much as scientists might expect. Tiny experimental detectors also uncovered surprising details about how radiation passes through the human body, offering valuable insights for future lunar exploration.
articles.summary: NASA's Artemis I mission has provided crucial data on cosmic radiation levels near the Moon, revealing higher exposure than in Earth orbit but manageable for future missions. This finding is essential for planning safe human lunar exploration.

articles.title: James Webb discovers a scorching lava planet with a “giant sunscreen”
articles.description: A scorching lava planet 280 light-years away has surprised astronomers by apparently maintaining a thick atmosphere despite conditions that should have stripped it away billions of years ago. James Webb Space Telescope observations suggest that TOI-561 b reflects about 75% of incoming starlight, possibly because of mineral clouds that act like a giant sunscreen. The planet may also be continually replenishing its atmosphere through gases released from a global ocean of molten rock.
articles.summary: The James Webb Space Telescope has discovered a distant lava planet 280 light-years away that surprisingly maintains a thick atmosphere despite extreme heat. This unexpected finding challenges our understanding of planetary atmospheres in extreme environments.

articles.title: See NASA's Artemis III astronauts meet Trump at the White House as they train for a critical 2027 moon lander test flight (photos)
articles.description: The astronauts of NASA's Artemis III mission met with President Trump at the White House on Wednesday (Oct. 28), just as the Artemis II spaceflyers did six months ago.
articles.summary: NASA's Artemis III astronauts met with President Trump at the White House as they prepare for a critical 2027 moon lander test flight, advancing humanity's return to lunar exploration.

articles.title: World's largest digital camera snaps new world beyond Pluto
articles.description: Space was so much simpler when I was a kid. Back in the 1980s, we still hoped to find habitable planets around every star. Nine planets orbited our own Sun. And “dwarf planet” sounded like a Saturday morning cartoon begging for its own toy line.Continue Readi…
articles.summary: The world's largest digital camera has discovered a new world beyond Pluto, expanding our understanding of distant solar system objects.

articles.title: The Rubin Observatory Finds Its First Dwarf Planet Candidate
articles.description: The Vera Rubin Observatory found a distant Solar System object before its decade-long Legacy Survey of Space and Time even got started. The object is a dwarf planet candidate named 2026 ED138, and if confirmed, it will be one of the largest dwarf planets beyo…
articles.summary: The Vera Rubin Observatory discovered its first dwarf planet candidate during early observations before its decade-long Legacy Survey of Space and Time begins.

articles.title: Astronomers Discover a Giant New Dwarf Planet Candidate Hiding Beyond Pluto
articles.description: What else could be out there?ScienceAlert stories are written, fact-checked, and edited by humans, never generated by AI. Don't miss a story, subscribe here.
articles.summary: Astronomers have identified a giant new dwarf planet candidate beyond Pluto, raising exciting questions about what other discoveries await in the distant solar system.

articles.title: A small star is eating a brown dwarf so slowly that the meal could last billions of years, and the two orbit each other every 87 minutes inside a space that would fit within the Sun
articles.description: A small red star is pulling gas from a brown dwarf as the pair circles every 87 minutes, packed into an orbit that could fit inside the Sun. Material strikes the star’s surface and lights up a hot spot, marking a meal that could continue for billions of years…
articles.summary: A red star and brown dwarf locked in an extraordinarily rapid 87-minute orbit demonstrate exotic stellar dynamics that could persist for billions of years.

articles.title: Artemis II : le voyage vers la Lune aurait pu capoter et s’est joué à quelques minutes, révèle l’un des astronautes
articles.description: Seulement cinq petites minutes : c'est la minuscule marge qui séparait l'équipage d'Artemis II d'un retour en catastrophe sur le plancher des vaches. Il ne s'en est fallu que de très peu pour que l'humanité rate son rendez-vous historique avec la Lune.
articles.summary: Artemis II astronauts revealed that their historic lunar mission came within five minutes of requiring an emergency return, highlighting the mission's critical precision.

Each day a different image or photograph of our fascinating universe is featured, along with a brief explanation written by a professional astronomer. Haunting the Cepheus […]
articles.summary: APOD features the Cepheus Flare, a stunning astronomical observation showcasing stellar formation and cosmic wonder in a distant region of space.
